newsitem.title: CHINA: Germany wants third China consulate, Kinkel says.
newsitem.headline: Germany wants third China consulate, Kinkel says.

text.p: Germany wants to set up a third China consulate in Chengdu, capital of the most populous province of Sichuan, German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday.
German officials said China was studying a request and they expected a favourable response.
"I think that another consulate in Chengdu is in German interests," Kinkel told reporters. "Before World War One, Germany had 18 consulates around China."
Germany now has consulates in Shanghai and the southern city of Guangzhou in addition to its embassy in Beijing.
Kinkel is on a fence-mending visit that was delayed by Sino-German differences over Beijing's policies in the restive region of Tibet.

The foreign minister had planned to visit in July but Beijing withdrew its invitation after the German lower house of parliament passed a resolution accusing China of trying to eradicate Tibet's cultural identity.
On Tuesday, Kinkel said that China and Germany had put their differences behind them and were now on a course for improved economic ties.
More than 100 million people live in Sichuan province, which is also home to heavy industry, much of it defence-related.
After the communists took power in 1949, they moved many of the nation's strategic industries into the interior -- including Sichuan -- in order to protect them from possible attack.

On Wednesday, Kinkel toured a Siemens AG joint venture factory that is producing optical fibre. After the visit, he told reporters such overseas ventures generally created more jobs for Germans than they lost.
The minister, who met President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng in Beijing on Tuesday, held talks with senior Sichuan provincial officials on Wednesday.
